We have a ImageJ plugin that analyzes images (microscope) and we would like it to send data to a R session to build dataframes.

We found how to start such things using Rcaller but I'm not sure it is the right way to do it. How would you do if you were me? I couldn't find a way to start JGR from Java, I found a script but no way to use R session. Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: Deducer talking and listening to ImageJ (or any other Java app)
messages.subject_clean: Deducer talking and listening to ImageJ (or any other Java app)
messages.body_plain:
There are two ways that you can set up communication with R:

The first is to have a stand alone Java app (i.e. ImageJ), and use
RServe to start-up and communicate with an instance of R.

The second is to have the user start you app from within an R session.
This is the Deducer way of doing things. Here you would just put the
ImageJ jar into an R package. When the user loads the package, ImageJ
will be available.

Last summer one of the Google Summer of Code projects looked at
creating a bridge between R and ImageJ. The code was never released to
CRAN, but I've attached the package here as it might be useful for
your project.

Best,
Ian

messages.subject: Re: apply the same
messages.subject_clean: apply the same
messages.body_plain:
To apply the same settings to several plots, you can save and re-use a template. More details here:
http://www.deducer.org/pmwiki/index.php?n=Main.PlotBuilder

To do multiple plots, with different variables (from the same data frame):

(a) if you want them all together as different "sub-plots" in the same figure, reshape your data frame so that all the variables are in the same column, and add a new column to distinguish your original variables; then use the "facets" of ggplot2 (available in Deducer's Plot Builder).

(b) if you want to do different plots in an automated procedure, you must write some code. Either a "for" loop or "lapply" the plot function across your data frame columns may work. You can see the code of a single plot done by Deducer in "Tools > View call" within the Plot Builder.

Helios

Hi JD,

I can't remember if the "color by" option was removed for Deducer
0.6-3, but it will be removed for version 0.7-0 due out on the third.
The templates are designed to be the simplest possible interface to
get standard plots. To create more colorful/rich plots, the grammar of
graphics is the way to go.

try building you histogram like you usually do, and the right click on
"histogram" in the component list on the right. Select "Break out." If
you now double click it, it will show you all of the histogram options
under the hood. drag a variable into "colour" and you will have your
stacked histogram.

ian
